\chapter{Communication Complexity — Public Coin One Way}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.PublicCoinOneWay
\section{Overview}

This module defines one-way public-coin protocols and their $\varepsilon$-error
communication complexity.  A public-coin protocol is modelled as a deterministic
one-way protocol whose input spaces are augmented with a shared randomness type
$\Omega$; correctness is measured by the probability (over the shared randomness)
that the protocol's output disagrees with the target function.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[One-way public-coin protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol}
A one-way public-coin protocol over shared randomness type $\Omega$ and
input types $X$, $Y$ with output type $\alpha$ is defined as a deterministic
one-way protocol whose Alice-input is $\Omega \times X$ and whose Bob-input is
$\Omega \times Y$.  The shared randomness $\omega \in \Omega$ is thus treated as
a component of both players' inputs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Protocol execution with shared randomness]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol}
Given a protocol $p$, inputs $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, and a shared random string
$\omega \in \Omega$, the execution $\mathrm{rrun}(p, x, y, \omega)$ runs $p$ on
the joint inputs $(\omega, x)$ for Alice and $(\omega, y)$ for Bob, returning
the decoded output $p.\mathrm{decode}(p.\mathrm{send}(\omega, x),\,(\omega, y))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-approximate computation]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun}
A protocol $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ if
for every input pair $(x, y)$ the measure of the set of shared strings on which
$p$ errs is at most $\varepsilon$:
\[
  \forall x,\, y,\quad
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega) \ne f(x,y)\}\bigr) \;\le\; \varepsilon.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape,
      CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes}
The $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of
$f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ is the infimum (in $\mathbb{N}_\infty$) of the
one-way message cost $p.\mathrm{cost}$ over all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all
protocols $p$ over the coin-tape space $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ that
$\varepsilon$-compute $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound characterisation]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape,
      CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost,
      CommunicationComplexity.Internal.enat_iInf_le_coe_iff,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{3}
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, and $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
the complexity satisfies $\mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon) \le m$ if and only if there
exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a protocol $p$ over $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that
$p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ and $p.\mathrm{cost} \le m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound characterisation]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.le_communicationComplexity_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape,
      CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{3}
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, and $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
the complexity satisfies $m \le \mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon)$ (as extended naturals)
if and only if every protocol $p$ over any $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ that
$\varepsilon$-computes $f$ has $p.\mathrm{cost} \ge m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity in error]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_mono}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\difficulty{4}
The $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of $f$ is
monotone non-increasing in $\varepsilon$: if $\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$ then
$\mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon) \le \mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon')$.  Intuitively, a
stricter error budget can only demand a larger protocol cost.
\end{theorem}
